 Common Judgment

These two petitions are filed by the Petitioners
U/s.166 of Mv Act, seeking compensation amount for
the injuries sustained by them in a road traffic
accident.

2.  The cases are arising out of one and same accident, the respondents are one and the same,
therefore, theses cases are clubbed to trial and dispose together to save the precious time of the court and to  SCCH-13 3 MVC.4822 & 4823/2023 avoid repetition of facts and to make convenient to the parties.

The evidence is led in MVC.No.4822/2023.
 3.

The brief facts of the case are that on 21.05.2023 about 9.40 a.m., when the petitioners were traveling on the motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53- EX-4762, as a rider and pillion rider towards Hosakote from H Cross Road, near Bharath Petrol Bunk, Lakshmipura Gate, Hosakote Taluk, Bengaluru Rual District, at that time, the driver of Mahendra Bolero vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-67-1652 (hereinafter called as offending vehicle) drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner motorcycle.

Due to the accident,
both Petitioners fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Further petitioners in both case immediately were taken to SNR District hospital Kolar, after first aid treatment petitioner in MVC.4822/2023 was shifted to Narendra Hospital, wherein he has taken treatment as inpatient and petitioner in MVC 4823/2023 as admitted as an inpatient at SNR District Hospital,
Kolar.
4. At the time of accident, the Petitioner in MVC.4822/2023 was working as a Mason and earning 25,000/-p.m.

Petitioner in MVC.4823/2023 was working as a Mason and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/-
p.m.

2 permanent disability and are unable to lead normal life as earlier and lost their earning capacity and income.

5. As the accident was due to negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle and as such,
the Respondent No.1 and 2 being the owner and insurer of the alleged vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
6. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before the court through their counsel and filed their objections.

7. Respondent No.1 - has denied all the averments of the petition inter-alia contending that the alleged accident has not occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, The  SCCH-13 5 MVC.4822 & 4823/2023 offending vehicle was insured with respondent No.2 and policy was valid as on the date of accident and the driver was holding valid DL and has prayed for dismissal of the petition.
 8.

The respondent no.2 has filed its written statement by admitting the issuance of policy to the alleged offending vehicle and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.
It has denied that the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
On the other hand, the accident has occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the petitioners.

REASONS  14.
Issue No.1 in both petitions:- Both Petitioners have examined as PW.1 & 2.

They say that on 21.05.2023 about 9.40 a.m., when they were traveling on the motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53- EX-4762, as a rider and pillion rider towards Hosakote from H Cross Road, near Bharath Petrol Bunk, Lakshmipura Gate, Hosakote Taluk, Bengaluru Rual District, at that time, the driver of the offending vehicle drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner  SCCH-13 8 MVC.4822 & 4823/2023 motorcycle. Due to the accident, both Petitioners fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
 15.
In order to prove the negligence of driver of the offending vehicle, Petitioners relied on the Police records.
PW1 and PW-2 has produced FIR, spot mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet at EX P1 to P6, and P15.
Based on first information statement, FIR was registered, mahazar was drawn and vehicles were got inspected and the charge sheet is filed against the driver of the offending vehicle.
Wound certificates of both the Petitioners have show that Petitioners both petition have sustained grievous injuries.
16. The respondent No.2 has contended that the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle and not on the part of the offending car.
17. Keeping in view of the arguments addressed by the learned counsel for the respondent once again I have perused the material available on record.

However on perusal of the charge sheet, complaint and FIR,
prima-facie establish that the accident occurred due to  SCCH-13 9 MVC.4822 & 4823/2023  the negligence on the part of driver of the offending vehicle and not on the part of the rider of the motor cycle.

Neither the respondent has challenged the charge sheet before any authority nor rebut the Venkateshappa vs Muniraja C N on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29465886/
5 evidence lead by the petitioner.

18. During the course of cross-examination of PW1 and PW2, learned counsel for the Respondent no 2 has put forth suggestion that the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle, who lost control and fell as the bike skid.
It is further suggested that the petitioners were not wearing the helmets at time of the accident.
They denied the same.

Further in the cross-examination of PW1 and 2,
it was suggested that the offending vehicle was not caused any accident, PW1 and PW2 in active collusion with police, have falsely implicated the offending vehicle.
They denied the same.

19. Except above said suggestion and contention raised in the objections, respondent no 2 -insurance  SCCH-13 10 MVC.4822 & 4823/2023 company has not produced any evidence to disprove the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
There are no materials on record to disprove the PW1 and PW2 testimonies and to prove the contention of the Respondents.
The testimonies of PW-1 and PW2 corroborated with the documents produced.
It is well settled principle that Motor Vehicles Act is beneficial legislation, the tribunal need not to go for the strict proof of rash and negligence.
After the investigation, police have filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle.
The material available on record probabalise that it was negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Thereby the accident occurred and petitioners have sustained injuries in a RTA.
Hence I answer Issue No.1 in both the petitions in the Affirmative.

So far as the compensation under non-pecuniary damages are concerned, considering the fact that the Petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and treated as an inpatient which caused him immeasurable mental agony and pain, I am of the opinion that an amount of .30,000/-

Under the pecuniary damages, expenses relating to treatment,
hospitalization and medicines, the Petitioner has relied  SCCH-13 15 MVC.4822 & 4823/2023 on medical bills for .1,20,068/- at Ex.P.11 and Ex.P21.
Though counsel for Respondent No.2 has cross-examined the PW-1, nothing has been elicited to disprove the medical bills.

32. Future Medical Expenses:
PW-3 has stated that the petitioner needs another surgery for removal of implant, which cost Rs.60,000/-.
But he has not produced any estimation report.
In the absence of material evidence, it is just and reasonable to award Rs.15,000/- towards future medical expenses.
33. Conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges:
Ex.P.8 - Discharge summary shows that Petitioner was treated as an inpatient at Narendra hospital, Kolar from 21.05.2023 to 29.05.2023 i.e. totally for a period of 9 days.

Therefore,
it is just and reasonable to award compensation of .15,000/- under the head of conveyance, food,
nourishment and attendant charges.
34. Loss of earning during laid up period:
With regard to loss of earnings during treatment, around 2 months for rest is considered and loss of earnings  SCCH-13 16 MVC.4822 & 4823/2023 during treatment is calculated for 3 months.

As the monthly income of the Petitioner is already considered as .16,000/- per month, loss of earning during laid up period would be .16,000 x 3 = 48,000/-.

These two petitions are filed by the Petitioners
U/s.166 of Mv Act, seeking compensation amount for
the injuries sustained by them in a road traffic
accident.
Due to the accident,
both Petitioners fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
4. At the time of accident, the Petitioner in MVC.4822/2023 was working as a Mason and earning 25,000/-p.m.
5. As the accident was due to negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle and as such,
the Respondent No.1 and 2 being the owner and insurer of the alleged vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
7. Respondent No.1 - has denied all the averments of the petition inter-alia contending that the alleged accident has not occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, The  SCCH-13 5 MVC.4822 & 4823/2023 offending vehicle was insured with respondent No.2 and policy was valid as on the date of accident and the driver was holding valid DL and has prayed for dismissal of the petition.
 8.
The respondent no.2 has filed its written statement by admitting the issuance of policy to the alleged offending vehicle and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.
On the other hand, the accident has occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the petitioners.
In order to prove the negligence of driver of the offending vehicle, Petitioners relied on the Police records.
Wound certificates of both the Petitioners have show that Petitioners both petition have sustained grievous injuries.
However on perusal of the charge sheet, complaint and FIR,
prima-facie establish that the accident occurred due to  SCCH-13 9 MVC.4822 & 4823/2023  the negligence on the part of driver of the offending vehicle and not on the part of the rider of the motor cycle.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Based on first information statement, FIR was registered, mahazar was drawn and vehicles were got inspected and the charge sheet is filed against the driver of the offending vehicle.
16. The respondent No.2 has contended that the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle and not on the part of the offending car.
There are no materials on record to disprove the PW1 and PW2 testimonies and to prove the contention of the Respondents.
The testimonies of PW-1 and PW2 corroborated with the documents produced.
It is well settled principle that Motor Vehicles Act is beneficial legislation, the tribunal need not to go for the strict proof of rash and negligence.
After the investigation, police have filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle.
The material available on record probabalise that it was negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Thereby the accident occurred and petitioners have sustained injuries in a RTA.
Due to the accident he has sustained grievous injuries.
He has stated that at the time of accident, he was working as a Mason and was earning Rs.25,000/-P.M.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is unable to do his work and is unable to do his work as earlier and suffering huge loss of income.
However, the petitioner has not produced any documents to substantiate his income.
In the absence of material with regard to source of income, the tribunal has to be considered the notional income chart of the Lok Adalath.
The alleged accident has taken place in the year 2023, the notional income of the injured could be assessed at Rs 16,000/- Per Month.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Hence, the Respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The policy was in existence as on the date of accident and hence  SCCH-13 23 MVC.4822 & 4823/2023 Respondent No.2-insurance company is liable to indemnify the claim of the injured Petitioners with interest @ 6% p.a.
53. Issue No.3 in both the petitions:
In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following:
 ORDER
Both claim Petitions filed under Sec.166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with cost.
Petitioner in MVC.4822/2023 is awarded compensation of 4,85,388/- together with interest @ 6%
p.a. (except future medical expenses) from the date of petition till the realisation.
Petitioner in MVC.4823/2023 is awarded compensation of 2,00,350/- together with interest @ 6%
p.a. (except future medical expenses) from the date of petition till the realisation.
Respondent No.2 shall deposit the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount in both the cases, entire amount with interest shall be released in favour of the Petitioners through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,000/- each.
Draw award accordingly.
